name: empty-containers
why: Empty object and array emit as {} and [] with no whitespace, at every nesting level.

name: key-ordering-utf16
why: Keys sort by UTF-16 code unit, NOT numerically and NOT by locale: "10" precedes "2" because '1' < '2', and uppercase precedes lowercase.

name: key-ordering-astral
why: UTF-16 code-unit order differs from CODE POINT order above the BMP: U+10000 begins with surrogate U+D800, which is BELOW U+FFFD, so the astral key sorts before it. Code-point sorting would place it last. This is the discriminator between a correct JCS sort and a plausible-looking one.

name: nested-objects
why: Sorting is recursive; inner objects sort independently of their position.

name: array-order-preserved
why: Arrays are semantically ordered; JCS never sorts them.

name: nfc-keys
why: Decomposed keys normalize to NFC BEFORE sorting: 'e'+U+0301 becomes U+00E9. Normalizing first is what makes the resulting order independent of input form.

name: nfc-values
why: String VALUES normalize too, so visually identical values from different input methods hash identically.

name: surrogate-pairs
why: Astral characters emit literally as UTF-8 4-byte sequences, not as escapes.

name: negative-zero
why: RFC 8785 renders -0 as 0 (ECMAScript Number::toString), so +0 and -0 are indistinguishable in the preimage.

name: numbers-rfc8785
why: The RFC 8785 number vectors: precision truncation, exponent switchover, trailing-zero removal.

name: exponents-extremes
why: Exponent-notation boundaries (1e20 vs 1e21, 1e-6 vs 1e-7) and the float64 extremes.

name: integers-and-floats
why: Integral values carry no decimal point; sign is preserved.

name: string-escapes
why: Shortest-form escapes for the five named controls, lowercase \uXXXX for other C0, and NO escaping of '/' or DEL (U+007F is not a control that JSON escapes).

name: literals
why: null / true / false at both object and array positions.

name: unicode-values-mixed
why: Non-ASCII values pass through as UTF-8, including CJK and the euro sign from the RFC example.
